seoDescription: Power system protocols on FPGA: a six-channel interpolated-DFT front end with CORDIC and ROCOF, wrapped in substation reporting protocols.

sections.heading: Power System Protocols
sections.body: Two messengers for the grid. An IEEE C37.118.1 phasor measurement unit that reports six channels at 50 frames a second, and an IEEE 2664-2024 (STTP) publisher that carries the same measurements over TCP with no processor anywhere in the datapath.

images.alt: A pigeon messenger in a red cap carrying a satchel

sections.heading: About this sketchbook
sections.body:
A PMU samples the grid's voltages and currents, turns each cycle into a phasor (magnitude, angle, frequency, rate of change) and stamps it with GPS time. The PMU is the pigeon: it writes the letter. The protocol is how the letter travels.

C37.118 is the classic fixed-frame carrier. STTP is the newer one: it compresses the measurements with TSSC and negotiates a subscription over TCP. Both are built here on the same ZCU106 board.
sections.kicker: note to self: the IpDFT front-end has its own case file →

sections.heading: IEEE C37.118.1 PMU
sections.body: A 6-channel, 3-phase PMU in VHDL on the PL fabric. Signal processing runs in hardware; C37.118 framing, config frames and UDP to the PDC run on the ARM PS.

sections.heading: IEEE 2664 · STTP
sections.body: A C37.118-class PMU and an STTP publisher entirely in programmable logic. No processor, no operating system, no software in the datapath: analog in one end, TCP/IP synchrophasor frames out the other. A stock, unmodified GPA cppapi subscriber decodes the stream.

sections.heading: Security
sections.body: Grid telemetry drives protection decisions, so a forged or delayed phasor is a physical risk. What these two designs defend against, and what they leave open, is written down in the repos rather than implied.

images.alt: A burglar with bolt cutters inside a red prohibition sign

items.label: No software to exploit
items.detail: STTP path: PS8 = 0, no MicroBlaze, no OS, no lwIP. The attack surface of a kernel and its libraries does not exist.

items.label: Deterministic timing
items.detail: Frames come from a fabric counter at 19.999 ms median. Nothing in the datapath can be starved or scheduled late.

items.label: Source provenance
items.detail: SHA-256 recorded for all 80 RTL sources, but 11 of 75 build entries were read from a /tmp path that no longer exists.

items.label: CRC is not a signature
items.detail: C37.118 frames carry CRC-CCITT. It catches corruption on the wire, not an attacker who recomputes it.

items.label: No TLS
items.detail: All STTP traffic is cleartext over TCP, verified across all three source trees the build reads.

items.label: No access filtering
items.detail: The connection string is ignored; all 14 points are served to any subscriber regardless of what it asks for.

items.label: Session can be taken
items.detail: One subscriber at a time. A second client or a capture tool can steal the session; a stale one blocks reconnect for ~60 s.

items.label: Time source
items.detail: The GPS / IRIG-B link passes 9/9 in simulation but was not connected during conformance; DataStartTime was free-running.

items.label: C37 path uses the PS
items.detail: The C37.118 design frames packets and runs UDP on Linux on the ARM, so it inherits that software surface.

sections.heading: Where the lock comes from
